title: Caught in 4K: The Aurora Files

reading.body:
This incident shows a general-purpose AI coding and agent tool being used as an operational component inside a ransomware attack chain. Cursor Agent, running Claude Sonnet, was directed by the attackers to carry out hands-on exploitation steps: installing VPN clients, scanning networks, enumerating domain privileges, and attempting credential relay attacks. The tool was not compromised or modified, it was used as intended by legitimate subscribers who happened to be criminals, placing the failure outside the AI system's own design and inside the absence of controls that would detect or block malicious use patterns at the application or account level.

The attackers also imposed their own guardrails on the AI, explicitly forbidding certain high-risk actions such as DCSync attacks and account lockouts. This shows the operators understood the tool's capabilities well enough to manage its behavior, treating it as a controllable asset rather than an unpredictable one. The failure mode is misuse of a deployed agentic system in conditions it was not built to police, specifically use by adversarial actors conducting intrusions against third-party networks, where no human checkpoint existed between the operator's instructions and the AI's execution of network and credential tasks.

What is not established is whether any of the ten or more organizations identified as targets experienced confirmed data loss or ransom payment, and the reporting does not establish the identity or location of the specific individuals operating Aurora.

reports.title: Russian-speaking cybercriminals used SpaceX’s Cursor AI tool to hack seven companies
Aurora ransomware targets ESXi, abuses Cursor Agent for exploitation

summary:
# Summary

Gambit Security's Threat Intelligence team identified Aurora ransomware operations targeting ESXi environments since April 2026. The group has deployed a Linux ransomware variant that encrypts virtual machine files while keeping the hypervisor bootable, allowing victims to see ransom demands. Attackers created a custom tool called esxi_finder.py to scan networks for ESXi hosts and vCenter servers. The research tracked ten target organizations affected between April and May 2026.

In a notable development, Aurora operators abused Cursor Agent, an AI tool running Claude Sonnet, to conduct hands-on exploitation tasks including installing VPN clients, scanning networks, enumerating domain privileges, and attempting credential relay attacks. Operators imposed strict restrictions on the AI, explicitly forbidding DCSync attacks, account lockouts, and adding new computer objects to domains. A separate cluster of activity, possibly involving different operators, targeted eight organizations across multiple countries using SQL Server vulnerabilities and S3 buckets for data exfiltration.
